*New AI laws now give platforms just three hours to remove deepfakes — or face massive fines.*

India’s AI regulation could quietly reshape how artificial intelligence content is controlled worldwide.

Starting February 20th, platforms must label AI-generated content and remove flagged deepfakes within a strict three-hour window. That timeline makes large-scale human review impossible — meaning automated systems will decide what stays up and what disappears.

This isn’t just about deepfakes. It’s about how AI regulation gets enforced when artificial intelligence is used to police AI-generated content — and how that may affect creators globally.

Inside:
• Why the three-hour rule changes platform behavior
• How compliance pressure increases content removal
• Why India may set the template for future AI laws
• What creators using AI tools should start doing now
